neighbours.label: A verb that takes a person object next, right before 'us/me/him/them' ('something to [cheer] me up', 'what [keeps] him going', 'what really [got] us excited', 'it definitely [got] our interest')
fire: A Midget team coming to test at the tunnel definitely got our interest, said the organizer.
As for what keeps him going twenty years after his first race, he says it is the crowd.
He went shopping for me and brought back something to cheer me up after a rough week.
What really got us excited was something called Quirkbot, a tiny robot kit for kids.
A lot of us can use something to cheer us up and keep us motivated this winter.
Searing seals in the juices, so that the meat stays moist, is a popular kitchen myth.
It was the music that kept them dancing until the lights came on at three.
Nothing could stop her now, and the thought of the prize kept her going all night.
quiet: A Midget team coming to test at the tunnel was announced on the website, said the organizer.
As for what he does twenty years after his first race, he says it is mostly farm work.
He went shopping for me and brought back something to eat after a rough week.
What really mattered was something called a budget, a simple sheet for the whole family.
A lot of us can use something to read and a quiet corner this winter.
Searing the steak in a hot pan, so that the crust forms, is a popular kitchen method.
It was the music that filled the hall until the lights came on at three.
Nothing could stop the train now, and the snow piled up on the tracks all night.

notes: The pole's output direction promotes object pronouns (them, him, us, me).
